teile.einleitung: Boleadoras, or bolas, are an ancient throwing weapon from South America. They consist of balls fixed to cords. They are best known as a tool of the gauchos, the cattle herders of the pampas.
wichtigste: Bolas consist of two or three balls on cords.
The cords are usually made of leather, and the balls are often stones covered in leather.
The gauchos used them to catch animals without killing them.
When thrown, the cords wrap around an animal’s legs.
The native peoples of South America used bolas long before the Europeans arrived.

abschnitte.text: Bolas consist of **two or three balls** hanging from long cords. The cords are joined together in the middle. The thrower swings the balls over their head and then lets go. In flight they spin, and when they hit an animal’s legs, **the cords wrap around them**. The animal stumbles and can no longer run away.

The **gauchos** were mounted cattle herders on the **pampas**, the wide grasslands of Argentina, Uruguay and southern Brazil. With bolas they caught cattle, horses and wild animals such as the **rhea**, a large flightless bird. The name comes from the Spanish word “bola”, which means “ball”. Today bolas are a symbol of gaucho culture and are often shown at festivals.

Bolas were not invented by the gauchos. The **native peoples of South America** hunted with them long before Europeans came to the land. Archaeologists have found old, worked **stone balls** in many places that were used for this. The gauchos took over the weapon and made it famous.

gewusst: A skilled thrower can hit a running animal from a long way away.
Because the animals were only tied up, they could be caught alive.

teile.einleitung: The Brahmaputra is one of the great rivers of Asia. It rises in Tibet, flows through India and Bangladesh and flows into the Bay of Bengal. On the way it has several names.
wichtigste: The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet, where it is called the Yarlung Tsangpo.
It breaks through the Himalayas in one of the deepest gorges on Earth.
In India it flows through a broad valley in the state of Assam.
In Bangladesh it is called the Jamuna and joins the Ganges.
In the river lies Majuli, one of the largest river islands in the world.
On its bank lies Kaziranga National Park, with many Indian rhinoceroses.

abschnitte.text: The Brahmaputra rises in the highlands of **Tibet**, north of the Himalayas. There it is called the **Yarlung Tsangpo** and flows from west to east for a long way. At the eastern end of the **Himalayas** it makes a great bend. In doing so it has cut an enormous **gorge**, which is regarded as one of the deepest on Earth. After that it flows south towards India.

In India the Brahmaputra flows through the state of **Assam** in the north-east. Here its valley is very wide, and the river often splits into many channels. Assam is famous for its **tea**, which grows on large plantations. In the river lies **Majuli**, one of the largest river islands in the world. Because of **erosion**, that is, the wearing away of land by water, it is getting smaller and smaller.

On the bank of the Brahmaputra lies **Kaziranga National Park**. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The largest population of **Indian rhinoceroses** in the world lives here. The Indian rhinoceros has only one horn and thick skin that looks like armour. Elephants, water buffalo and tigers also live in the park.

After India, the Brahmaputra flows into **Bangladesh**, where it is called the **Jamuna**. There it joins the **Ganges**. Together the rivers form a huge **delta** on the **Bay of Bengal**. In the rainy season, the **monsoon**, the river carries an enormous amount of water. Floods then often occur, but they also bring fertile mud to the fields.

gewusst: The name Brahmaputra means “son of Brahma”, after a god in Hinduism.
The Brahmaputra flows through three countries: China (Tibet), India and Bangladesh.

teile.einleitung: A fault-block mountain range forms when the Earth’s crust breaks into large blocks. These blocks, called fault blocks, are raised, lowered or tilted. Well-known examples are the Black Forest, the Vosges and the Harz.
wichtigste: Fault-block mountains form when blocks of crust are raised or tilted along faults.
A raised block is called a horst, a lowered one a graben.
The Black Forest and the Vosges form the shoulders of the Upper Rhine Graben.
A block raised on one side only, like the Harz, is called a tilted block.
When the crust is stretched, normal faults form.
Basel lies at the southern end of the Upper Rhine Graben.

abschnitte.text: The outer layer of the Earth, the **Earth’s crust**, is not completely rigid. If it is stretched or squeezed, it can break along **faults**. A fault is a break surface along which blocks of rock move against each other. The individual blocks are called **fault blocks**. They can be raised, lowered or **tilted**. This is how a fault-block mountain range forms.

A block **raised** between faults is called a **horst**. It lies higher than its surroundings. A block that has **sunk** is called a **graben**. Both typically form when the crust is **stretched**. A block then slides down along a sloping surface, which is called a **normal fault**. If a block is strongly raised on one side only, it is called a **tilted block**, a bit like a writing desk. Examples are the **Harz** and the **Ore Mountains**.

Between Basel and Frankfurt lies the **Upper Rhine Graben**. As the graben sank, its edges were pushed up. To the east lies the **Black Forest**, and to the west the **Vosges**. The basement rock of the Black Forest is a remnant of the **Variscan mountains**, which formed about 300 million years ago in the **Carboniferous**. They were worn away and later raised again as a fault block.

**Basel** lies at the southern end of the Upper Rhine Graben. Here the crust is still moving today. In **1356**, a severe earthquake shook the city. It is regarded as the strongest historically recorded earthquake north of the Alps. Many buildings collapsed, and fires destroyed large parts of the city. That is why, to this day, people in the Basel region pay special attention to earthquake-proof building.

In the west of the USA, especially in **Nevada** and **Utah**, lies the **Basin and Range** region. There the crust is being stretched and breaks into many parallel blocks. Raised horsts form mountain ranges, and sunken grabens form basins. The **Sierra Nevada** in California is a tilted fault block: in the east it is steeply raised, and towards the west it slopes down gently.

gewusst: In some places the Upper Rhine Graben is filled with over 3,000 metres of deposits.
Because the crust is thin, the ground in the Upper Rhine Graben is warmer in some places than elsewhere.

teile.einleitung: Lignite, also called brown coal, is a brown, soft fuel from the ground. It was formed from plants that grew in swamps and bogs millions of years ago. Lignite is younger than hard coal and gives less energy.
wichtigste: Lignite is geologically younger than hard coal.
It contains more water and therefore gives less energy per kilogram.
Lignite is mostly mined in open-cast mines.
It is mainly burned in power stations to generate electricity.
Burning it produces especially large amounts of CO2.

abschnitte.text: Many millions of years ago, dense forests grew in **swamps and bogs**. Dead plants sank into the water and were covered by mud and sand. Without air, they did not rot completely. Under the pressure of the layers above, they first became **peat** and then **lignite**. If it stays deep in the earth for much longer, it can become **hard coal**.

Lignite is **geologically younger** than hard coal. It is softer, often crumbly, and contains a lot of **water**. For this reason it gives **less energy** per kilogram when burned. It is therefore not transported far, and power stations are often built right next to the pits. Lignite usually lies not very deep and is mined in **open-cast mines**, with huge excavators under the open sky.

Lignite is mainly burned in **power stations** to produce **electricity**. This produces especially large amounts of **CO2**, more than most other ways of generating electricity. Whole villages sometimes have to make way for open-cast mines. Germany has decided to stop generating electricity from coal by 2038 at the latest. In Switzerland, too, some lignite used to be mined, for example in the **Käpfnach mine** in Horgen, which is now a museum.

gewusst: The bucket-wheel excavators in big lignite mines are among the largest land vehicles in the world.
In lignite you can sometimes still find remains of wood, leaves and tree trunks.

teile.einleitung: Brazil is the largest country in South America. It is known for the Amazon rainforest, for football and for the carnival. People in Brazil speak Portuguese, because the country was a Portuguese colony for a long time.
wichtigste: Brazil is the largest country in South America, and its capital is Brasília.
In the 2022 census, around 203 million people were counted.
The largest city is São Paulo.
The official language is Portuguese, and the currency is the real.
Brazil has won the men’s football World Cup five times (as of 2026).
The flag is green with a yellow diamond and a blue globe.

abschnitte.text: In area, Brazil is the **largest country in South America** and one of the largest in the world. It borders almost all the other countries of the continent. The **equator** crosses the north of the country, and the **Tropic of Capricorn** passes just by **São Paulo**. In the north lies a large part of the **Amazon rainforest**, the largest rainforest on Earth. The capital is **Brasília** in the interior.

In the **2022** census, around **203 million** people were counted. That is more than twenty times as many as in Switzerland. The largest city is **São Paulo**, with over 11 million inhabitants, the largest city in all of South America. **Rio de Janeiro** is also very well known, with the statue of Christ on a mountain above the city. The people of Brazil have ancestors from Europe, Africa, Asia and among the indigenous peoples.

Brazil was for a long time a **Portuguese colony**. That is why **Portuguese** is the official language, while most neighbouring countries speak Spanish. Brazil became independent in **1822**. Since 1994 people have paid with the **real**. The flag is **green** with a **yellow diamond**. In the middle is a **blue globe** with stars and a band with the motto “Ordem e Progresso”, meaning “Order and Progress”.

Football is very popular in Brazil. The men won the World Cup **five times**: in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002 (as of 2026). No other country has won more often. The most famous player was **Pelé**. He became a **three-time world champion**, in 1958, 1962 and 1970. No other player has managed that.

The **carnival** takes place every year before Lent. In Rio, **samba schools** parade with enormous floats and colourful costumes along a specially built street, the Sambadrome. **Capoeira** also comes from Brazil. This martial art looks like a dance and is practised to **music and singing**. It was developed by people of African descent.

gewusst: Brazil is the largest coffee producer in the world.
On the border with Argentina lie the mighty Iguazú Falls.
Brazil has more Portuguese-speaking inhabitants than Portugal itself.

teile.einleitung: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina. The large port city lies on the Río de la Plata, a very wide river mouth. The city is famous for the tango, for colourful houses and for very wide streets.
wichtigste: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina and lies on the Río de la Plata.
The people of Buenos Aires are called Porteños, meaning “port dwellers”.
A landmark is the Obelisk, about 68 metres tall.
The Avenida 9 de Julio is regarded as one of the widest streets in the world.
In the La Boca district, many houses are painted in bright colours.
The president has his seat in the Casa Rosada.

abschnitte.titel: City on the Río de la Plata
abschnitte.text: Buenos Aires lies on the **Río de la Plata**, a very wide mouth of the rivers Paraná and Uruguay. On the other side lies the country of **Uruguay**. The city is an important **port**. That is why its inhabitants call themselves **Porteños**, which means “port dwellers”. The name Buenos Aires means “good airs” or “fair winds” in Spanish.

In the middle of the city stands the **Obelisk**, a white tower about **68 metres** tall. It is a landmark of Buenos Aires. It stands on the **Avenida 9 de Julio**, which is regarded as one of the **widest streets in the world**. It has many lanes in each direction. On foot, you need several sets of traffic lights to cross it. Its name recalls 9 July 1816, the day of Argentina’s independence.

In the **La Boca** district, many houses are painted in bright colours. In the past, people used **leftover paint from the port** for this. La Boca is also home to the stadium of the well-known football club Boca Juniors. The **tango** arose on the Río de la Plata in the 19th century, a dance and a kind of music that is now known all over the world. Many immigrants from Italy and Spain shaped the city.

The seat of the Argentine **president** is called the **Casa Rosada**, which means “pink house”. Because of its colour the building is easy to recognise. It stands on the **Plaza de Mayo**, the most important square in the city. Many large gatherings and demonstrations have taken place here in Argentina’s history.

**Pope Francis** came from Buenos Aires. His name at birth was **Jorge Mario Bergoglio**, and he was born in the city in **1936**. Before he became pope, he was Archbishop of Buenos Aires. He was the **first pope from the Americas** and the first from the Jesuit order.

gewusst: The Teatro Colón in Buenos Aires is regarded as one of the most important opera houses in the world.
The tango of the Río de la Plata is part of UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage.

teile.einleitung: Blood diamonds, also called conflict diamonds, are diamonds whose sale pays for armed conflicts. Rebel groups used the money to buy weapons. The Kimberley Process was created to stop this trade.
wichtigste: The money from blood diamonds is used to pay for armed conflicts.
In Sierra Leone, the rebel group RUF paid for its civil war from 1991 to 2002 in this way.
In Angola, UNITA financed its fight with diamonds for decades.
The Kimberley Process certification system has applied since 2003.
It is named after the town of Kimberley in South Africa.
Critics point out that it does not cover violence committed by states.
Botswana is seen as an example of how diamonds can help development.

abschnitte.text: Diamonds form deep in the **Earth’s mantle** under great pressure and heat. They reach the surface in volcanic pipes made of **kimberlite**. This is where the **primary deposits** lie. Rivers can also wash diamonds out of the rock and leave them in **alluvial ground**. Such deposits are called **alluvial**. There, diamonds can be mined with just a shovel and a sieve, without expensive equipment.

Because alluvial diamonds are so easy to mine, rebels were able to raise money with them. In **Sierra Leone**, the **Revolutionary United Front** (RUF) controlled diamond fields in the east of the country during the civil war from 1991 to 2002. In **Angola**, the rebel movement **UNITA** sold raw diamonds worth billions of dollars during the civil war. The groups used the money to buy weapons, and the wars lasted longer. Ordinary people suffered greatly as a result.

In 2000, diamond-producing countries met in **Kimberley** in South Africa, a historic centre of diamond mining. This led to the **Kimberley Process**. Its certification system has applied since **2003**. Raw diamonds that are traded need a **certificate of origin** confirming that they do not come from conflict zones. Switzerland also takes part in the Kimberley Process.

A common criticism of the Kimberley Process is that it only covers **rebels**. Human rights abuses by **governments**, for example in the Marange diamond fields in Zimbabwe, do not fall under the rules. A positive example is **Botswana**. The country uses its diamond income, earned through the joint company **Debswana** with the firm De Beers, to pay for schools, health care and roads.

gewusst: Diamond is the hardest natural material and is made only of carbon.
A rough diamond often looks plain, like a cloudy pebble, and only cutting makes it sparkle.

teile.einleitung: BRICS is a group of countries that want to work together more closely. The name comes from the first letters of the first members: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Other countries have joined since.
wichtigste: The economist Jim O’Neill coined the abbreviation BRIC in 2001.
South Africa joined later, and so it became BRICS.
In 2014 the countries founded the New Development Bank, based in Shanghai.
At the start of 2024, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, among others, joined.
In January 2025, Indonesia became a full member.
The group wants to give the global South more weight in the world economy.

abschnitte.text: In 2001, the economist **Jim O’Neill** of the bank Goldman Sachs grouped **Brazil, Russia, India and China** together under the abbreviation **BRIC**. He meant countries whose economies might become especially important in future. The idea later grew into real cooperation between the governments. From 2009 the heads of state met at summits. **South Africa** joined as a further country, and the name became **BRICS**.

abschnitte.titel: Its own bank and reserve fund
abschnitte.text: At the summit in Fortaleza in Brazil in 2014, the countries decided to set up the **New Development Bank**. It is based in **Shanghai** and finances projects for infrastructure and sustainability. At the same time the **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** was created, a joint fund. It is meant to help members that are short of foreign currency for a short time.

At the start of 2024 the group grew: **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran** and the **United Arab Emirates** joined. Argentina turned down an invitation. In January 2025, **Indonesia** joined as the first country in Southeast Asia. Other countries have shown interest in cooperating.

The BRICS countries want the countries of the **global South** to have more say in the world economy. They see themselves as a **counterweight** to groups such as the G7 and to organisations such as the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. BRICS is not, however, a formal organisation with a fixed treaty. The members have very different political systems and sometimes pursue different interests. Observers therefore judge the importance of the group in different ways.

gewusst: A large part of the world’s population lives in the BRICS countries together.
The chairmanship of the group rotates every year between the members.

teile.einleitung: Borneo is the third largest island in the world. It lies in Southeast Asia and is largely covered in rainforest. Three countries share the island: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
wichtigste: After Greenland and New Guinea, Borneo is the third largest island in the world.
The island is about 18 times as big as Switzerland.
Three countries share Borneo: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
The Indonesian part is called Kalimantan and covers about three quarters of the island.
Orangutans, proboscis monkeys and hornbills live on Borneo.
Brunei became rich through oil and natural gas.

abschnitte.text: Borneo lies in **Southeast Asia**, between Java, Sulawesi and the Philippines. About three quarters of the island belong to **Indonesia** and are called **Kalimantan**. In the north lie the Malaysian regions of **Sarawak** and **Sabah**. Between them lies the small **Sultanate of Brunei**. In Brunei a sultan rules, that is, a ruler with great power.

Large parts of Borneo are covered in **tropical rainforest**. It is one of the oldest rainforests on Earth and is home to a huge variety of species. Many areas have been cleared, however, mainly for **oil palm plantations**. In the north rises **Mount Kinabalu**, the highest mountain on the island at a good 4,000 metres. Its area is a national park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

**Orangutans**, large apes with reddish fur, live on Borneo. The **proboscis monkey** is found only here. The males have a very large, hanging nose. In the sky fly **hornbills**, which have a growth on the beak like a horn. They also live in other parts of Asia and in Africa.

The **rafflesia** has one of the largest flowers in the world. It has no leaves and no stem and lives off another plant. Its flower smells of rotting meat and so attracts flies. **Pitcher plants** have cup-shaped traps filled with liquid. Insects slip inside and are digested. In this way the plants get nutrients that are missing from the soil.

Tiny **Brunei** produces a lot of **oil** and **natural gas**. As a result, people there have a high income and pay no **income tax**. In Switzerland, by contrast, people pay income tax to the municipality, the canton and the Confederation. In Kalimantan, Indonesia is also building a new capital called **Nusantara**.

gewusst: The equator runs right across Borneo.
The rafflesia grows not only on Borneo but also on other islands in Southeast Asia.
Borneo is one of the few places in the world where orangutans live in the wild.

teile.einleitung: The Bonnet Carré Spillway is a large flood relief structure on the Mississippi in the USA. When the river is in flood, it diverts water above New Orleans into Lake Pontchartrain. In this way it protects the city from flooding.
wichtigste: The Bonnet Carré Spillway lies on the Mississippi in the state of Louisiana.
In a flood it diverts water into Lake Pontchartrain.
When it is opened, the water level of the Mississippi at New Orleans falls.
It was built after the great Mississippi flood of 1927.
It is operated by the US Army Corps of Engineers.

abschnitte.text: A **spillway** is a relief weir, in other words an overflow. If the **Mississippi** rises too high, the Bonnet Carré Spillway is opened. Part of the water then flows off sideways through a wide channel into **Lake Pontchartrain**. From there it continues into the Gulf of Mexico. This lowers the **water level** at **New Orleans** and takes pressure off the levees.

In **1927** there was a huge flood on the Mississippi. Large areas were under water, and very many people lost their homes. Afterwards it was decided to control the river better. The Bonnet Carré Spillway was built over the following years and finished in the early 1930s. The weir consists of many bays with **wooden beams**. To open it, they are lifted out with cranes.

Lake Pontchartrain normally contains **brackish water**, that is, slightly salty water. When the spillway is open, a lot of **fresh water** flows in from the river. This can harm animals that are used to salty water, for example **oysters**. For this reason the spillway is only opened when it is really necessary.

gewusst: In 2019 the spillway was opened twice in the same year for the first time.
Switzerland also has relief tunnels that carry floodwater past towns.

teile.einleitung: Slash-and-burn means that forest is burned down to make room for fields or pasture. The ash fertilises the soil for a short time. It is a very old method, but today it often has serious consequences for nature and the climate.
wichtigste: In slash-and-burn farming, forest is burned to gain farmland or pasture.
The ash fertilises the soil, but rain quickly washes the nutrients away.
In shifting cultivation the whole settlement moves on, in rotational farming only the fields move.
In English this way of using land is called shifting cultivation.
In the Amazon region, cleared land mostly becomes cattle pasture.
Burning releases CO2 that was stored in the forest.

abschnitte.text: First trees and bushes are felled or cut into, then everything is **burned**. The **ash** contains nutrients and fertilises the soil. In the first few years, harvests are therefore good. In the tropics, however, it often rains heavily. The rain **washes the nutrients** away quickly, and after a few years the yields drop sharply.

Many peoples in the tropics have lived from this method for centuries. In **shifting cultivation**, people move their fields and also their **settlement**. In **rotational farming**, the village stays in the same place and only the fields change. The old plots are abandoned and grow over again. In English this way of using land is called **shifting cultivation**. Millions of people around the world live from it.

abschnitte.titel: When the rest period gets too short
abschnitte.text: For soil and forest to recover, many years of **fallow** are needed, that is, a time without farming. If the population grows, more land is needed. Plots are then used again too soon. The fallow periods become too short, and the soils are **permanently impoverished**. In this way a sustainable method becomes a problem.

Today forest is often cleared on a very large scale. In the Brazilian **Amazon region**, cleared land mostly becomes **pasture for cattle**. Growing **soya** also plays an important part. In **Indonesia** and **Malaysia**, huge **oil palm plantations** are created on cleared rainforest. Palm oil is found in many foods and cosmetics. The fires there sometimes cause heavy smoke over whole regions.

Trees store **carbon**. When they burn, it enters the air as **CO2** and worsens climate change. In addition, the forest is no longer there afterwards as a **carbon store**. With the forest, the habitats of many animals and plants disappear too. In Europe, too, forest was once turned into farmland by burning, for example in the Middle Ages.

gewusst: The soils of many rainforests are rather poor in nutrients, despite the lush plants.
Smoke from forest fires in Southeast Asia can drift into neighbouring countries and force schools to close there.

teile.einleitung: Brain drain means that well-educated people leave their country and work abroad. For the country they come from this can be a loss, and for the country they move to it can be a gain.
wichtigste: Brain drain is the emigration of highly qualified people abroad.
The term arose in the 1960s for British researchers who moved to the USA.
The opposite is called brain gain, the gain for the destination country.
With brain circulation, knowledge also flows back to the country of origin.
Brain waste means that qualified people work below their level of training.
In 2024, around 40 per cent of doctors in Switzerland had a foreign diploma.

abschnitte.text: The British **Royal Society** used the expression **brain drain** in the 1960s. At that time, many British scientists moved to North America because they found better conditions there. Later the term was applied mainly to **poorer countries**, from which doctors, engineers or researchers emigrate to richer countries. The reasons are often higher wages, better jobs or more security.

The destination country experiences a **brain gain**: it gains skilled workers whose training it did not pay for. With **brain circulation**, skilled workers return or keep close contact with their homeland, so both countries benefit. People speak of **brain waste** when, for example, a trained doctor works as a cleaner. The cause is often that her foreign **diploma** is not recognised.

Some experts, including **Oded Stark**, put forward the idea of the **beneficial brain drain**. It says that the prospect of work abroad motivates more people to get a higher **education**. Because not everyone actually emigrates, the number of qualified people in the country of origin can rise overall. Other experts are more critical. The question is still debated today.

Brain drain is especially noticeable among **doctors and nurses**. When they go abroad, hospitals are short of staff, particularly in rural areas of poor countries. In 2010 the **World Health Organization** (WHO) therefore adopted a voluntary **code of practice**. It is meant to prevent rich countries from deliberately recruiting staff from countries that have a shortage.

**Switzerland** benefits greatly from skilled workers from abroad. According to the doctors’ statistics of the FMH, in 2024 around **40 per cent** of practising doctors had a foreign diploma, most of them from Germany. In 2009 the European Union introduced the **EU Blue Card**. With it, highly qualified people from non-EU countries can work in the EU more easily.

gewusst: Money that emigrants send to their families back home is an important source of income for some countries.
Brain drain also happens within a country, for example when young people move from mountain valleys to the cities.

teile.einleitung: The Burgess Shale is a famous fossil site in the Rocky Mountains in Canada. It lies in Yoho National Park and is a good 500 million years old. Even soft-bodied animals from the Cambrian have been preserved here.
wichtigste: The Burgess Shale lies in Yoho National Park in British Columbia, Canada.
The rocks date from the Cambrian and are a good 500 million years old.
Soft parts are preserved too, which is very rare among fossils.
The site was discovered in 1909 by Charles Walcott.
The animals date from the time of the Cambrian explosion.

abschnitte.titel: A window into the distant past
abschnitte.text: Usually only the **hard parts** of animals, such as bones, teeth or shells, are left as fossils. In the Burgess Shale it is different. Here **soft parts** are preserved too, such as legs, gills or even the gut. The animals were probably buried quickly by fine mud that contained hardly any oxygen. This meant they did not rot completely. The rock is called **shale** because it can be split into thin plates.

The animals lived in the sea in the **Cambrian**. During this time, many new animal forms appeared in a short time. This is called the **Cambrian explosion**. In the Burgess Shale you find peculiar creatures. **Opabinia** had five eyes and a long trunk with a grasping claw. **Anomalocaris** was a large predator with grasping arms on its head. Most common is **Marrella**, a small arthropod.

The American researcher **Charles Walcott** discovered the site in **1909**. Over the following years he collected tens of thousands of fossils. Today the Burgess Shale is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, as part of the parks of the Canadian Rocky Mountains. Visitors may only visit the sites on guided tours, so that nothing is damaged.

gewusst: One animal from the Burgess Shale was given the name Hallucigenia because it looked so strange.
The site lies high in the mountains, although the animals once lived in the sea.

teile.einleitung: Bolivia is a country in the heart of South America. It has high mountains, huge salt flats and tropical forests. Bolivia has no coast and is named after the freedom fighter Simón Bolívar.
wichtigste: According to the constitution the capital is Sucre, while the government and parliament sit in La Paz.
Bolivia is landlocked and has no access to the sea.
The country is named after Simón Bolívar and became independent in 1825.
The constitution names 37 official languages: Spanish and 36 indigenous languages.
Bolivia calls itself a “plurinational state”.
Lake Titicaca lies on the border with Peru.

abschnitte.text: Bolivia has an unusual arrangement: **Sucre** is the capital according to the constitution. The government and parliament, however, are based in **La Paz**. La Paz lies at over 3,500 metres and is considered the highest seat of government in the world. Visitors notice the thin air, and many people need a few days to get used to it.

Bolivia once had a coast on the Pacific. In the **War of the Pacific** in the 19th century, it lost this region to **Chile**. Since then Bolivia has been **landlocked**. Even so, it has a navy. It sails mainly on **Lake Titicaca** and on the big rivers in the lowlands. Bolivia has never given up its wish for access to the sea.

Many **indigenous peoples** live in Bolivia, that is, descendants of the people who lived there before the Spaniards. The constitution therefore names **37 official languages**: Spanish and 36 indigenous languages such as **Quechua**, **Aymara** and **Guaraní**. The country calls itself a **plurinational state**, a state of many peoples. Switzerland also has several national languages, but only four.

Bolivia was for a long time a **colony of Spain**. In the 19th century, **Simón Bolívar** led several countries of South America to independence. When Bolivia became independent in **1825**, it was given his name. Under the Spaniards, the city of **Potosí** was famous for a mountain of silver. Huge amounts of **silver** were dug out of the earth there.

In the west rise the **Andes** with the highland plateau, the **Altiplano**. This is where the **Salar de Uyuni** lies, the largest salt flat in the world. Beneath the salt are large reserves of **lithium**, which is needed for batteries. In the east the land becomes flatter and warmer, and tropical forests grow there that belong to the Amazon region.

gewusst: Bolivia and Paraguay are the only countries in South America with no access to the sea.
The Salar de Uyuni is so flat that after rain it looks like a gigantic mirror.
Lake Titicaca lies at over 3,800 metres above sea level.

teile.einleitung: A boomerang is a curved, flat throwing stick. Aboriginal Australians have used it for a very long time. Some boomerangs fly back to the thrower in an arc after being thrown, while others keep flying straight.
wichtigste: A boomerang is a curved, flat throwing stick.
Aboriginal Australians used it mainly for hunting.
Only light returning boomerangs come back to the thrower.
Heavy hunting boomerangs fly far and straight.
In flight a boomerang spins quickly around itself.

abschnitte.text: A boomerang is a **curved, flat piece of wood**. The **Aboriginal peoples**, the native people of Australia, have used such throwing sticks for a very long time. In the past they were mainly used for **hunting**, for example birds. Boomerangs were also used as a **tool**, for digging or making fire, and as a **toy**. Similar throwing sticks were also known in other parts of the world, for example in ancient Egypt.

Not every boomerang comes back. The heavy **hunting boomerangs** fly **far and straight** to hit an animal. The light **returning boomerangs**, on the other hand, fly in a big **arc** and come back to the thrower. They are less suitable for hunting and better for play and competitions.

A thrown boomerang **spins quickly around itself**. Its arms are curved like the **wings of an aeroplane**. This creates **lift** as it flies, which keeps it in the air. Because the boomerang is spinning, this lift is not equally strong everywhere on its arms. This steers it a little to the side all the time, and so it flies a **curve**. If you throw it correctly, the curve ends at the thrower.

Today throwing boomerangs is also a **sport**. There are competitions in which you have to throw as accurately, as far or for as long as possible. Modern sports boomerangs are often made of **plywood** or **plastic**. Throwing needs space and care, because a boomerang flying back can hurt people.

gewusst: A returning boomerang is thrown almost upright, not flat like a frisbee.
There are boomerangs with three or four arms that also fly back.

teile.einleitung: The United States of America is made up of 50 states. Each state has its own capital, its own parliament and its own laws. This is a little like the cantons of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The USA is made up of 50 states.
The smallest state by area is Rhode Island.
California has the most inhabitants (as of 2024).
A state’s capital is often not its largest city, for example Austin in Texas.
Four states border Mexico and 13 border Canada.
At the Four Corners, Utah, Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico meet.

abschnitte.text: The USA is a **federal state** made up of **50 states**. Each has a **governor**, its own parliament and its own courts. Many things, such as schools or criminal law, are decided by the states themselves. The capital of the whole USA, **Washington, D.C.**, does not belong to any state. The 50 stars on the flag stand for the 50 states. In a similar way, in Switzerland the Confederation and the **cantons** share the tasks.

The **smallest** state by area is **Rhode Island** on the east coast. At about 4,000 square kilometres, it has only about a tenth of the area of Switzerland. The largest is **Alaska** in the far north. **California** has the most inhabitants, with about 39 million people in 2024. **Texas** comes second.

In the USA the capital of a state is often **not the largest city**. The capital of **Texas** is **Austin**, not Houston. In **California** the government sits in **Sacramento**, not in Los Angeles or San Francisco. And the capital of the state of **New York** is **Albany** on the Hudson River. New York City is much bigger, but it is not the seat of government.

Many states have **nicknames**. Texas is called the “**Lone Star State**” because its flag shows a single star. It recalls the time from 1836 to 1845, when Texas was an independent republic. **Michigan** consists of two large **peninsulas** between the Great Lakes. The **Mackinac Bridge** joins the two parts.

Four states border **Mexico**: California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas. Thirteen states border **Canada**, from Alaska in the west to Maine in the east. This border is regarded as the longest land border in the world. At the **Four Corners**, **Utah**, **Colorado**, **Arizona** and **New Mexico** meet at right angles at a single point. This does not happen anywhere else in the USA.

gewusst: Hawaii was admitted in 1959 as the last of the 50 states.
Every state sends exactly two members to the Senate, no matter how big it is. In a similar way, in Switzerland every canton has two seats in the Council of States.

teile.einleitung: Bonaire is a small island in the Caribbean, north of Venezuela. It belongs directly to the Netherlands, where it is a “special municipality”. Bonaire is known for its coral reefs, flamingos and salt.
wichtigste: Bonaire lies in the Caribbean off the coast of Venezuela.
Since 2010, Bonaire has been a special municipality of the Netherlands.
Sint Eustatius and Saba also have this status.
Aruba and Curaçao are separate countries within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
The main town is called Kralendijk.

abschnitte.titel: A piece of the Netherlands in the Caribbean
abschnitte.text: Until 2010, Bonaire belonged to the **Netherlands Antilles**. When these were dissolved, a new arrangement was chosen. **Bonaire**, **Sint Eustatius** and **Saba** became **special municipalities** of the Netherlands. Together they are also called the **Caribbean Netherlands**. **Aruba** and **Curaçao**, on the other hand, are separate countries within the kingdom. People on Bonaire pay with the **US dollar**.

Around Bonaire lie colourful **coral reefs**. They are protected, and the island is popular with divers from all over the world. Many **flamingos** live on the island, searching for food in shallow salt lakes. In the south, **salt** has been produced for a long time by letting seawater evaporate in the sun. The white mountains of salt can be seen from far away.

Most people on Bonaire speak **Papiamentu**, a language that developed from Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch and African languages. Dutch is also used. The main town is **Kralendijk**. Because it rarely rains on Bonaire, many **cacti** grow there.

gewusst: In the south of the island stand small stone huts that recall the time of slavery in the salt works.
Bonaire lies outside the usual zone where hurricanes strike the Caribbean.

teile.einleitung: Brasília is the capital of Brazil. It was built in only about four years in the middle of the country and was inaugurated in 1960. From above, its layout looks like an aeroplane or a bird.
wichtigste: Brasília was inaugurated as the new capital on 21 April 1960.
Before that, Rio de Janeiro was the capital from 1763 to 1960.
President Juscelino Kubitschek drove the building forward.
The city plan, the Plano Piloto, was designed by Lúcio Costa.
The striking buildings are by the architect Oscar Niemeyer.
Since 1987, Brasília has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: For a long time **Rio de Janeiro** on the coast was the capital. The idea of building a new capital in the **interior** came early on. This was meant to help the interior of Brazil grow too. President **Juscelino Kubitschek** carried out the plan. He promised “50 years of progress in 5”. After only about four years of building, Brasília was inaugurated on **21 April 1960**.

The city planner **Lúcio Costa** won the competition for the city plan, the **Plano Piloto**, in 1957. Two crossing axes give it the shape of an **aeroplane** or a **bird**. The **Monumental Axis** forms the body, where the government and ministries stand. The curved **Residential Axis** forms the wings. There lie large residential blocks with schools, shops and green spaces.

The architect **Oscar Niemeyer** created the curving buildings made of **concrete**. Very well known is the **cathedral**, whose supports reach upwards like hands. The **National Congress** has two domes, one opening upwards and one downwards, and two tall office towers. Niemeyer wanted buildings that look light and elegant.

Brasília lies on a **plateau** more than 1,000 metres above sea level. It is drier here than on the coast. When the city was built, a river was **dammed**. This created the artificial **Lake Paranoá**. It was meant to make the climate more pleasant and today is also used for recreation, such as sailing and swimming.

Since **1987**, Brasília has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. It is one of the youngest cities on this list. The city is honoured as a unique example of 20th-century **urban planning**. Around the Plano Piloto, many more settlements have grown up in the meantime, and most of the people in the region live there.

gewusst: Brasília was built where there had been no city before.
Oscar Niemeyer lived to be over 100 and worked into old age.

teile.einleitung: Bossa nova is a gentle style of music from Brazil. It began in Rio de Janeiro in the late 1950s. Bossa nova combines the rhythm of samba with the sounds of jazz.
wichtigste: Bossa nova began in Rio de Janeiro in the late 1950s.
The style combines samba with jazz.
Quiet singing and a guitar are typical.
Important musicians were João Gilberto and Antônio Carlos Jobim.
The best-known song is “Garota de Ipanema”.

abschnitte.text: In Portuguese, “bossa nova” means roughly “new style” or “new wave”. Unlike the loud samba of the carnival, bossa nova sounds **calm and soft**. Usually a **guitar** plays a special, slightly off-beat rhythm. Someone sings quietly over it, almost whispering. **Jazz** brought special chords that give the style its soft sound.

The singer and guitarist **João Gilberto** shaped the typical rhythm. The composer **Antônio Carlos Jobim** wrote many famous songs, often with the poet **Vinícius de Moraes**. An early, important song is “Chega de Saudade” from 1958. The music grew up in the flats and bars by the beaches of Rio, for example in **Copacabana** and **Ipanema**.

The best-known song is “**Garota de Ipanema**”, named after a beach in Rio. In English it is called “The Girl from Ipanema”. In the early 1960s, bossa nova also became very popular in the USA and in Europe. Jazz musicians all over the world played the songs. To this day, bossa nova is often heard in cafés, hotels and films.

gewusst: “Garota de Ipanema” is one of the songs that have been recorded anew most often around the world.
João Gilberto played so quietly that listeners in the concert hall often had to stay completely silent.

teile.einleitung: The Brenner Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel that runs under the Alps and links Austria and Italy. It runs from Innsbruck to Fortezza (Franzensfeste) in South Tyrol. Together with the Innsbruck bypass, it will be the longest underground railway link in the world.
wichtigste: The tunnel links Innsbruck in Austria with Fortezza in Italy.
The main tunnel measures about 55 kilometres.
Together with the Innsbruck bypass, the underground section is over 60 kilometres long.
This makes it longer than the 57-kilometre Gotthard Base Tunnel.
It is expected to open around 2032 (as of 2025).
An exploratory tunnel lies beneath the two main tubes.

abschnitte.text: The **Brenner Pass** lies at about **1,370 metres** above sea level on the border between Austria and Italy. It is one of the lowest crossings over the Alps. That is why a **railway line** and a **motorway** already cross the pass today. A great many lorries drive on the road. The new **base tunnel** passes beneath the pass deep inside the mountain, so that trains can run with almost no gradient.

The main tunnel runs from **Innsbruck** to **Fortezza** in South Tyrol and measures about **55 kilometres**. At Innsbruck it joins an existing bypass tunnel. Together this gives an underground section of **over 60 kilometres**. That is more than the 57 kilometres of the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** in Switzerland, which opened in 2016.

The tunnel consists of **two main tubes**, one for each direction of travel. A few metres below lies an **exploratory tunnel**. During construction it shows what the rock inside the mountain is like. Later it is used for **drainage** and carries mountain water away. Between the tubes there are cross-passages so that people can reach the other tube in an emergency.

An earlier opening was originally planned. **Geological difficulties**, that is, difficult rock inside the mountain, delayed the construction. According to current plans, the tunnel is due to open **around 2032** (as of 2025). The aim is to move more **goods from road to rail**. Switzerland pursues the same idea with its Alpine tunnels.

gewusst: The Brenner Base Tunnel is part of a major European railway axis from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean.
In the tunnel, the border between Austria and Italy is crossed deep inside the mountain.
